results.comment: Badly Drawn Turtle People can be very rational. Being rational is just a way of thinking, in this context basing your judgment on the evidence and things relevant to the case presented in court rather than prejudice or outside knowledge.  While people can often be stupid, experience suggests that people actually take their role on juries quite seriously.  And computers would be great at being jurors if you could assign mathematical values to evidence. But you can't. Example:  V was shot, allegedly by D, on the corner of Bert St and Russell St at around 9pm. A, who was walking his dog at the time, says he saw a man wearing a black hoodie and jeans, with what A believes was a gold watch, shoot V at close range, and then run off. The police searched D's house and found that he owns a black hoodie and jeans. D also wears a watch.
